explanation: I grepped Mathlib for dist/edist bounds on integrals, using the patterns `dist_integral`, `dist (∫` and `norm_integral_sub_le`. The only match with a similar shape is `MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.dist_integral_le_lintegral_edist` in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/VectorMeasure/Integral.lean. It is stated for vector-measure integrals ∫ᵛ with a bilinear map B. Its bound has an extra factor ‖B‖ and integrates against μ.variation. Deriving the scalar-measure statement from it would mean building a vector measure and a bilinear map, which is not a short instantiation. Its proof also uses the same steps as the target (dist_eq_norm, integral_sub, norm_integral_le_lintegral_norm), so it is a parallel result rather than a source for this one. The Bochner-side `edist_integral_le_lintegral_edist` in the same file is derived from the target, so it is circular.
